newsitem.title: USA: Tulsa Vo-Tech district seeks tax exempt bond issue.
newsitem.headline: Tulsa Vo-Tech district seeks tax exempt bond issue.

text.p: The Tulsa County Area Vo-Tech school district's proposed $37.5 million lease revenue bond issue will be considered Friday by the Oklahoma Finance Authorities (OFA) for granting it a double-tax exempt status, an official said Monday.

Jim Buie, vice president of OFA, a state public trust, said the tax status will exempt the 20-year bonds both from state and federal income taxes, and that OFA approval will give the securities greater credit enhancement and insurance.
The bonds will be supported by a building tax levy set up under the country's property tax.

The Vo-Tech district, a nationally-recognized system for vocational and technical training, is seeking the bond issue to finance the relocation of its aviation training facilities at Tulsa's R.L. Jones Riverside Airport to meet a growing demand for aviation-related training.

The district, which serves students from 14 school districts in Tulsa and other counties in northeastern Oklahoma, plans to construct a new 280,000 square-foot campus at the airport. The 24.7 acre land for the campus will be acquired from the Tulsa Airport Authority.
Buie said the bonds will be sold in the second week of August.
T.J. Thompson & Associates Inc., and Leo Oppenheim and Associates, both of Oklahoma City, wil be the co-managers of the issue.
"Right now, there is good demand for double-tax exempt lease revenue bonds and we are hoping the interest rate will come in below 5.5 percent," Buie said.
